articles.title: Why did 3 SET senator-members favor Erwin Tulfo’s ouster?
articles.summary: 'Justice and fairness went out of the window when three minority senator-members voted in favor of an out-of-time motion for reconsideration filed by a petitioner without legal standing,' says…

blocks.text: ERWIN TULFO. Senator Erwin Tulfo pushes for stronger protections for persons with disability (PWDs) during the hearing of the Committee on Social Justice, Welfare and Rural Development on Monday, October 19, 2026.
Senate of the Philippines

'Justice and fairness went out of the window when three minority senator-members voted in favor of an out-of-time motion for reconsideration filed by a petitioner without legal standing,' says Senator Ping Lacson

The Senate Electoral Tribunal’s (SET) decision to affirm the dismissal of a petition to unseat Senator Erwin Tulfo over alleged citizenship issues was largely anticipated — the March ruling was anchored on insufficiency in form — but the votes of three senator-members favoring Tulfo’s ouster was not.

In a statement signed by SET Secretary Luis Jose Geronimo, the tribunal said it denied the motion for reconsideration (MR) filed by petitioner Berteni Causing, seeking to reverse its March 2 ruling summarily dismissing his quo warranto petition for being “insufficient in form.”
The SET said the MR was filed beyond the prescribed period and “failed to comply with the filing and service requirements of the 2020 SET Rules.”

The nine-member tribunal convened at the Senate on Friday, October 16, with the Supreme Court (SC) justices and senator-members in attendance. Six SET members voted to deny the MR, while three opposed the dismissal, reportedly minority senators Robin Padilla, Pia Cayetano, and Camille Villar.

SC Senior Associate Justice Marvic Leonen chairs the SET, with SC justices Henri Jean Paul Inting and Ramon Paul Hernando serving as members. Senators Kiko Pangilinan, Bam Aquino, and Lito Lapid represent the majority bloc in the tribunal while Padilla, Cayetano, and Villar represent the Senate minority.

“Let’s give credit to the three SC justice-members and the other three senator-members who undoubtedly knew the obvious procedural flaw which resulted in a 6-3 vote, thus dismissing the MR,” Senator Panfilo “Ping” Lacson said over the weekend.
Lacson, without naming the three minority senators, questioned their decision to favor what he described as an “out-of-time MR filed by a petitioner without legal standing.”

“Justice and fairness went out of the window when three minority senator-members voted in favor of an out-of-time motion for reconsideration filed by a petitioner without legal standing,” Lacson said in a social media post.
“Their motive may be deeper than personal issues against Sen Tulfo,” he added.
Tulfo has repeatedly clashed with minority senators in the months spanning Alan Peter Cayetano’s tumultuous Senate presidency, the subsequent leadership change, and the ongoing impeachment trial.

In June, Tulfo called out then-Senate president Alan, calling him “thick-skinned” for skipping Senate session for a second consecutive day, along with minority senators, preventing the upper chamber from holding sessions due to a lack of quorum. At the time, Cayetano said they would not attend the session to keep control of the Senate blue ribbon committee and other panels.

During the impeachment trial, Tulfo questioned whether the proceedings were the proper venue for senator-judges to discuss their personal legal issues. This came after Padilla denied allegations that he had ignored an Ombudsman order related to complaints accusing him of obstruction of justice.
Tulfo also figured in a heated exchange with Villar during a debate on whether to revisit the threshold for convicting an impeachable official.

Villar took offense and became emotional when she defended colleagues from Tulfo’s remarks that the framers of the 1987 Constitution did not anticipate that future senator-judges could face corruption-related cases, such as plunder and theft.
Asked to comment on the 6-3 vote at the SET, Tulfo did not confirm the names of those who voted against him but said he was “hurt.”

“We were hurt. As you can see, we were all interacting with each other and then suddenly, they will do that. We’re a bit sad but that is their right. I mean, what can we do?… Kung ‘yun ang pananaw nila, then so be it. Ipagpasa-Diyos na lamang natin (If that is their view, then so be it. I leave it up to God),” he said in an interview on Monday, October 19.
Tulfo was more candid on Facebook, where he shared an editorial illustration depicting himself being stabbed in the back by knife-wielding arms labeled “Sens. Padilla, Villar, Pia.”
“Nakita ko lang (I just saw this)…. tsk, tsk, tsk,” he said in his post on Saturday, October 17.
What other “deeper motive” could there be, as suggested by Lacson? Where could a senator’s removal from office have any significant impact?

If one were to consider the impeachment trial, had the SET removed Tulfo from office, the number of active senator-judges participating in the trial would have fallen to 19. Based on the denominator, 15 votes would have been needed to convict Duterte, while five votes would have resulted in her acquittal. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Teodoro seeks higher capital outlay for 2027 to boost defense coverage
articles.summary: The Department of National Defense (DND) on Monday is seeking higher capital outlay under its 2027 budget as it seeks to build additional infrastructure that would bolster the country"s security…

blocks.text: Published October 19, 2026 5:14pm

The Department of National Defense (DND) on Monday is seeking higher capital outlay under its 2027 budget as it seeks to build additional infrastructure that would bolster the country’s security capabilities.

The National Expenditure Program provides for a P324.632 billion budget for the Defense Dept. next year. Of which, P32,671,776 is allotted for capital outlay, a decline from the P43,148,125 approved for this year.
Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. said that the capital outlay is the armed forces’ “biggest gap.”

“We need a lot of infrastructure right now, particularly on the eastern sea board, where we do not have naval presence. We do not have substantial infrastructure in Palawan, not for the naval purposes, but for the army purposes, which will serve as hubs for supporting our strategic bases,” he told the Senate Committee on Finance during the budget deliberations.
The defense chief also noted that there is only one Army brigade for the province of Mindoro and a single infantry division to secure Northern Luzon.

“So we really need to refocus our strategic positioning in these areas and we cannot do that until, sustainably, until the Army solidifies its footprint in the Philippines,” said Tedoro. “So capital outlay is extremely important also for building critical infrastructure facilities for security of our platforms and security of our operations.”
Moreover, Teodoro said the DND is eyeing building hubs in various parts of the country to help the defense forces’ mobility.
“So our mobility is sacrificed. We cannot bridge the whole of the Philippines, but the best we can do is to provide hubs, as many hubs as possible, which will support sustained operations,” he said.
Further, the department expressed its interest to have reserves for oil products.

“We are busy building up our reserve, not only in terms of ammunition, but we need it also in terms of petroleum, oil, and lubricants. We have big notional amounts of petroleum ready, but if we do not have physical custody of this, we will be relying on private gas stations to serve our needs, which is a vulnerability of our operating troops,” said Teodoro. —RF, GMA News

articles.title: Three months of experience with an ergonomic vertical mouse
articles.summary: If you get wrist strains, this could be up your alley

blocks.text: All of my previous mice were cheap, wired, office mice. One of them succumbed to pandemic-era Minecraft gameplay. While I was using its replacement, I heard about vertical mice: uniquely fin-shaped peripherals that allegedly cure desk-worker wrist strain.

My wrist hurt when I held my mouse the normal way, so I took a leaf out of this and started holding them from the side… as much as I was able. Eventually, my last mouse started ghost-clicking, and I wanted to see if shaking hands with a real vertical mouse was the ergonomic miracle it claims to be.

So I grabbed a knowledgeable friend, checked out online resources, and bought a promisingly named Go Comfy W195R from Fantech. And three months into using this mouse, my wrist and hand are much happier.

Relax your arms and drop them to your side: your palms will face your body. If you drop your relaxed arms on a desk, your palms will be perpendicular to the surface. Sure, you could twist your wrist to make your palm lie flat, like you would for a typical mouse, but maintaining that for a long time will keep you in an unnatural position.

A vertical mouse is built off your natural arm posture by having its body on the side rather than the top. This structure allows you to grip the mouse from the side, retain your palm’s curve, and keep your wrist untwisted.

The Fantech Go Comfy W195R is designed just like that. I got used to the shape quickly not just because it felt comfortable, but also because I was already holding mice like this. My pointer finger appreciates not having to stretch to reach the left click. At approximately 114 grams, the Go Comfy W195R is slightly heavier than my previous mouse, though it didn’t feel too different.

The mouse fits the shape of my hand well, and my wrist doesn’t ache anymore. My thumb, on the other hand, gets a mild strain if on the thumb rest for too long, which I’ve resolved by resting it above the side buttons and giving my hand a break. I’ll take that over my poor wrist.

All my previous mice were wired mice, so I didn’t have to charge or replace batteries. The Go Comfy W195R, however, is exclusively a wireless or Bluetooth connection. At first, I was sad to lose the convenience of being able to just plug it in, but I see the appeal of wireless now. There’s less clutter on my desk, and I can hold my mouse as near or as far as I like. I can even use my mouse from my couch.

I prefer to use my mouse wirelessly with the USB dongle, but I can also quickly switch it to the Bluetooth connection. In one moment, I could use it on my laptop, then I can toggle Bluetooth and connect it to my tablet.

The mouse uses an optical sensor, whose red light dims when it detects it’s no longer on a working surface. I’ve been flashed by my previous mice’s optical sensors when I held them up, so I find this to be a nice touch.
The left and right buttons are noticeably softer and silent, but the side buttons are clickier.

The plastic upper half of the mouse where the buttons are gathers dirt easily. When I run my finger over it, I can feel specks of dirt and dust, so I have to clean and wipe it frequently. It can be a bit annoying, but I see this as a bit of a silver lining: it reminds me to keep my mouse clean. I didn’t feel specks on my previous mice, so I dread to think of how dirty they actually were.

I’m right-handed, and my mouse is definitely for a right-handed person because of where the main buttons are. If you’re left-handed and looking for a vertical mouse, note that while left-handed vertical mice do exist, they’re harder to find.

I’ve shown my mouse to other people with different hands, and while my mouse fits my small hand, it does not fit bigger hands. I got lucky here as I neglected to check the size of the mouse before buying. This is a bit hard to check online since you can’t hold it, but online listings should show the dimensions.

Lastly, these ergonomic mice are built to strain you less while you use them, but they won’t stop strains entirely nor are the sole source of your strains. Be sure to have proper posture and to take breaks and stretch regularly.
If a vertical mouse suits you, here’s where you can buy it. – Rappler.com

This piece was written by Rappler intern Czarina Yasmin Sia. Czarina is an earnest creator whose works focuses on the little things and helping others. She enjoys engaging with unconventional ways to tells stories and is eager to write about life’s overlooked aspects. A graduating Communication Arts student from De La Salle University Manila, she aims to inspire people to find wonder.

articles.title: Possible wreckage of Amelia Earhart's plane likely to be trees, say researchers
articles.summary: Researchers travelled to a remote Pacific Island to confirm whether an object first spotted on satellite imagery in 2020 solved the mystery of the pilot's disappearance.

blocks.text: Image source, Archaeological Legacy Institute
A satellite image of the so-called Taraia Object, which some had hypothesised could have been Amelia Earhart's plane, in a lagoon on Nikumaroro
Researches looking at what they thought could have been the wreckage of Amelia Earhart's plane on a remote Pacific island say it is likely to be washed up trees.

The team travelled to a lagoon in the Taraia Peninsula on Nikumaroro, Kiribati, to confirm whether a shiny object first spotted on satellite imagery in 2020 solved the decades-long mystery of the pioneering pilot's disappearance.
But Purdue University, which has a leading role in the study, said the so-called Taraia Object "was likely a collection of large trees deposited along the peninsula's sandspit".
By the time the team arrived at the site a good portion of the debris had fragmented and washed away, leaving only a single Y-shaped segment, the university said.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Amelia Earhart disappeared over the Pacific Ocean while piloting her Electra plane in 1937

blocks.text: Image source, Getty Images
Amelia Earhart disappeared over the Pacific Ocean while piloting her Electra plane in 1937

Images of the Taraia Object - which Purdue University said was visible in photography dating back to 1938 - led researchers to wonder if it was the remnants of a small aircraft sitting in shallow waters.
"This mystery has been ongoing for 90 years and the mystery continues," said project director Rick Pettigrew, speaking from near the site of the object.
"The island has been holding on to its secrets and it continues to do so. I think eventually someone will find conclusive evidence here," he added.

blocks.caption: A satellite image of Nikumaroro Island in the Pacific Ocean showing the location of the Taraia Object

blocks.text: Earhart's plane vanished without a trace in 1937 on the third-to-last leg of her attempt to fly around the world.
She had already successfully flown from California across South America, Africa and Asia in her twin-engine Lockheed Electra when she arrived in Lae, Papua New Guinea.
Earhart and her navigator Fred Noonan had planned to then travel towards Hawaii before returning to California.
But their plane vanished while trying to reach Howland Island, a remote uninhabited coral island about 400 miles (644km) from Nikumaroro, to refuel.
One theory is Earhart unintentionally navigated to Nikumaroro, where she ditched her plane and died a castaway.
The research team had travelled for five days by sea to reach Nikumaroro and was forced to spend several days on their ship following rough seas and strong winds, delaying their search on the island.
They spent four days onshore investigating the site.

blocks.caption: Map showing the relative locations of Papua New Guinea, Hawaii, Australia, Howland Island and Kikumaroro Island

articles.title: Rodante Marcoleta placed under preventive suspension for 90 days
articles.summary: The Sandiganbayan Third Division has placed Senator Rodante Marcoleta on preventive suspension in connection with the plunder charge he is facing before the anti-graft court over alleged undeclared…

blocks.text: Published October 19, 2026 5:09pm

The Sandiganbayan Third Division has placed Senator Rodante Marcoleta on preventive suspension in connection with the plunder charge he is facing before the anti-graft court over alleged undeclared campaign contributions worth P75 million.
The anti-graft court said the suspension issued on October 19 is anchored on the Plunder Law (Republic Act 7080) and the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act (Republic Act 3019).

“There is no requirement for a pre-suspension hearing before an accused can be preventively suspended in a case of plunder under the court's Internal Rules or in jurisprudence,” the anti-graft court said.

“The provisions on preventive suspension under the Plunder Law and the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act are worded similarly, and both laws provide that preventive suspension is mandatory when there is a valid information,” it added.

Likewise, the Sandiganbayan said the plain reading of the factual allegations in the informations, when hypothetically admitted, sufficiently constitute the elements of plunder and violation of Presidential Decree 46 prohibiting public officials from receiving gifts.
The same resolution states that Marcoleta will automatically be lifted upon the expiration of the 90 days from the suspension’s implementation.

Marcoleta’s co-accused in the case include the alleged donors of the P75 million, namely former Anakalusugan party-list Rep. Mike Defensor, as well as businessman Joseph Espiritu and Aristotle Viray. –NB, GMA News

articles.title: Safety concerns mount over Japan’s traditional festivals after string of fatal accidents
articles.summary:
Deputy mayor of Saijo died after becoming trapped under float, days after two similar incidents elsewhere

There is mounting concern over the safety of Japan’s traditional festivals after the…

blocks.text: There is mounting concern over the safety of Japan’s traditional festivals after the death of a senior local official who was reportedly crushed beneath a float at the weekend, days after two men died in similar incidents in another part of the country.

Akihiro Nabae, the deputy mayor of Saijo, in western Japan, was carrying a giant float with other participants in a festival on Saturday when he became trapped beneath the structure, Agence France-Presse reported. Nabae, 62, was taken to hospital and later pronounced dead, local media said, adding that no one else was injured.

He died less than two weeks after a 51-year-old man was crushed beneath a wooden float he was riding at one of the annual Danjiri festivals held in southern Osaka prefecture. The same day, a 48-year-old man was killed in a similar accident at a Danjiri event in a nearby town. Police said 16 people were injured in the incidents.

blocks.caption: Participants push and pull a float during the Danjiri festival celebrations in Anan, Tokushima. Photograph: Keiichi Miyashita/AFLO/Shutterstock

blocks.text: The accidents occurred when the floats, which can weigh up to 4 tonnes, toppled as they were being pulled at speed around tight corners by hundreds of men, police said. The turns, known as yarimawashi, are a highlight of the festivals, originally held to pray for good autumn harvests.
It is not clear if Nabae lost his balance or if the contraption toppled on to him, according to police in Saijo, where the festival has been held annually since the Edo period (1603-1868).
Media reports said 11 floats, each weighing as much as 3 tonnes, were lined up side by side at the time of the accident.
The annual Saijo festivals, featuring more than 100 floats, are held to thank Shinto deities for plentiful grain crops, the Jiji news agency said.

blocks.caption: The floats weigh up to 4 tonnes each. Photograph: Keiichi Miyashita/AFLO/Shutterstock

blocks.text: Saijo’s mayor, Mitsuyoshi Ochi, voiced shock and sadness at Nabae’s death. “Just when we were about to work together to build a new administration for Saijo, this tragedy occurred. I still can’t believe it. I offer my heartfelt condolences,” he said in a statement.

In February, two people died in a crush at the “naked man festival” in Okayama, where as many as 10,000 men dressed in fundoshi loincloths squeeze into the grounds of a temple and compete to seize a pair of sacred wooden sticks thrown into the crowd by the head priest. The two men who succeed are declared “lucky men” for the year.

articles.title: Need a document notarized? Supreme Court launches online service
articles.summary: The public can now notarize their documents online through three accredited platforms.

blocks.text: October 19, 2026 | 5:01pm
The logo of the Supreme Court at the Supreme Court Building in Manila.
Philstar.com / Ian Laqui
MANILA, Philippines — Electronic notarization (e-notarization) was officially launched by the Supreme Court on Monday, October 19.
According to the Supreme Court, the public can now notarize their documents online through three accredited platforms.
The accredited platforms are as follows:

items: Twala
QLegal
NotarizeIT

blocks.text: For any platform, one must prepare:

items: A valid, unexpired Philippine National ID or government-issued ID.
A working device with a camera and microphone.
A stable internet connection of at least 2 Mbps per user.
An up-to-date browser such as Chrome, Edge, Safari, or Firefox.
The document in PDF or PDF/A format.
An email address for account creation and platform notifications.

blocks.text: A person seeking e-notarization must also disable their VPN, proxy, or Tor, as these can interfere with location verification.

The validity of each electronically notarized document has the same "validity, force, and effect and may be relied upon to the same extent as any other notarial act performed under the 2004 Notarial Rules."
However, electronic notarization does not apply to the execution of documents that require wet signatures, according to the Rules of Electronic Notarization.
Examples of these documents include notarial wills, depositions, and paper documents and instruments with wet signatures or marks.

A person seeking electronic notarization also cannot use ordinary Zoom, Google Meet, or Microsoft Teams for the notarization itself; the act must be performed through a Supreme Court-accredited e-notarization platform.
Specific requirements for each platform can be accessed on the Supreme Court website.

articles.title: Inconsistent guidelines for AI use in N.S. classrooms fuel calls for provincewide policy
articles.summary: Nova Scotia does not have a provincewide policy explicitly stating how AI should be used in the classroom. The provincial government says it’s up to regional centres for education to make their own…

image.caption: Jenna Poste is a parent and member of a national advocacy group, Skills Before Screens. The group aims to re-think how technology is being used in schools. (Grey Butler/CBC)

blocks.text: Nova Scotia

Nova Scotia does not have a provincewide policy explicitly stating how AI should be used in the classroom. The provincial government says it’s up to regional centres for education to make their own rules about the technology. Parents and educators are calling for more consistency, and say guardrails are needed.
Expert says teachers need to be 'judicious' with how they allow their students to use AI

Jenna Poste is not opposed to artificial intelligence — in fact, she uses it all the time as someone who works in the tech industry. But as a parent, she’s highly concerned about how, when and why it’s being introduced to young people.

In Nova Scotia, there is no provincewide policy explicitly stating how AI should be used in the classroom. The provincial government says it’s up to regional centres for education to make their own rules about the technology.
“We need to have consistency,” said Poste, a member of the national advocacy group Skills Before Screens. “We should really be taking a cautious approach.
“We shouldn’t be pushing forward like we have with our other technologies. We just assume it’s going to be helpful to learning without actually having the data that supports it.”
Why parents worry about their kids using AI in school
CBC News reached out to the regional centres for education, as well as the francophone school board, to ask about their AI policies. Their approaches vary.

For example, the Halifax and Chignecto-Central regional centres for education have guidelines in writing, while in the Cape Breton-Victoria district, use of AI varies by grade level and teachers must “use their judgement.”

items: Once labelled a 'cheating machine,' AI cautiously embraced in Halifax schools
New Brunswick is weaving AI into its K-12 curriculum, drawing praise — and pushback

blocks.text: The Annapolis Valley Regional Centre for Education said it “follows provincial curriculum and guidance” from the Department of Education, and has an educational technology team to support teachers and school staff.

The South Shore and Tri-County regional centres for education said they are focused on ensuring students learn the fundamentals, while they are “actively monitoring the emergence of AI in education to identify potential opportunities.”

The Strait Regional Centre for Education is finalizing a plan to provide AI guidelines and resources for students and staff. The Conseil Scolaire Acadien Provincial does not currently have a policy, but has appointed a committee to develop one.
Chris Boulter is the senior executive director for Nova Scotia's Department of Education and Early Childhood Development. (CBC)
Chris Boulter, senior executive director for the Department of Education, said the government strives to ensure students across the province have similar experiences no matter where they live.
Asked whether the department will develop provincewide guidelines for AI in classrooms, he said it's an "ongoing conversation." He said officials are monitoring what other jurisdictions are doing.
Boulter emphasized the department's primary focus is to ensure students have literacy, math and critical thinking skills.

"We feel that sets them up very well to use artificial intelligence to improve their learning," he said. "But again, I can't stress enough, those foundational skills have not gone away because of AI. If anything, it's caused us to really double down on our efforts."

Peter Day, president of the Nova Scotia Teachers Union, said many of his members have reverted to in-class assessments on paper because it’s not uncommon for students to hand in work that’s been obviously generated by a chatbot.
He said AI cannot exist in the school system without guardrails in place.

Peter Day is president of the Nova Scotia Teachers Union. He says many teachers have gone back to in-class assessments because some students use AI chatbots to complete their assignments. (Grey Butler/CBC)
He compared it to students being taught how to safely use a bandsaw in an industrial arts class before they're given free reins to try out the tool.
“I don’t see AI as that much different. I think we really need to be showing students how AI works and what an appropriate use for it would be.”

But in order to teach students how to use AI responsibly, Day said teachers have to feel confident in their own skills. Apart from a voluntary summer technology camp, he said there is no provincewide professional development focused solely on AI for educators.

items: Manitoba ban on social media, AI chatbots for kids could start in schools: education minister
Why these parents want to see less screen time in N.S. classrooms

blocks.text: Boulter said professional development is currently available through regional centres for education, but work is underway to develop more learning opportunities for teachers through the province.

Johan Woodworth, an assistant professor who teaches courses on AI integration and literacy at Mount Saint Vincent University’s education program, said educators have to be “judicious” with how they allow their students to use AI.
Not only can it replace critical thinking and shortcut learning, he said, but it can also produce outputs that are biased, misleading or even factually incorrect.
Johan Woodworth is an assistant professor with Mount Saint Vincent University's education program. He teaches courses on AI integration and literacy. (Eric Wiseman/CBC)
Woodworth also insists that a provincewide policy is needed. Like Day, he said teachers need more time and resources to become familiar with the tools.
“Just knowing about a technology doesn’t mean that you could pedagogically integrate them into a classroom,” he said.

He pointed to New York City — home to the largest school district in North America — where officials recently imposed a one-year moratorium on generative AI up to Grade 8, while chatbots in schools have been banned for all grades.

items: Free course covering basics of AI to be available to all Canadians by end of the year
Could AI really 'kill all humans'? Breaking down the dire warnings about the technology's existential risk

blocks.text: “The tech industry wants us to believe that AI in early education is not only inevitable, but that it is necessary. We do not see it that way,” New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said at a press conference in September.

Woodworth argues that a similar approach could benefit Nova Scotians, giving teachers an opportunity to catch up with the booming technology while policymakers evaluate best practices and develop rules.
Poste is pushing for that kind of pause through Skills Before Screens, which has launched a petition calling on the province to follow New York’s lead.
“I think there’s always a place you can find an opportunity where it could be beneficial. It’s just, do those benefits outweigh the risks?” Poste said.

articles.title: Rising use of AI-staged real estate photos raises questions about misleading homebuyers
articles.summary: If you've been looking to buy a home in Ontario, you may have seen a few listings where the furniture doesn't look quite right. That's because many of them are being staged virtually, using AI.…

blocks.text: Toronto

If you've been looking to buy a home in Ontario, you may have seen a few listings where the furniture doesn't look quite right. That's because many of them are being staged virtually, using AI. Experts say there are benefits and drawbacks of the tool.
In Ontario, virtual staging is governed under existing regulations around advertising
That perfect Ontario real estate listing might be staged by AI. Here's what to watch for

If you’ve been searching for a home in Ontario, you may have come across a listing where the furniture doesn't look quite right or where the size of the rooms is noticeably different in person than online.

Artificial intelligence is making it increasingly easy for real estate agents and sellers to virtually stage properties — adding furniture, artwork and decor to listing photos without physically moving a single item.

The technology offers an affordable way to help prospective buyers envision how they might use an empty space, and there are advertising rules in place to protect them. But real estate experts warn altered images could mislead buyers in some cases.
“The biggest challenge with AI staging is space,” said Ravi Singh, a real estate agent with RE/MAX Hallmark Realty.

“You might take a look at a photo and think 'OK, that easily fits a love seat, sofa, coffee table and end tables.' And then you walk into an empty space, and you say, 'Wait a second, how on earth did all that fit?'” Singh said.
“It's easy to do online, it's different to stage in person.”

Ravi Singh, a real estate agent at REMAX Hallmark Realty Ltd., says virtual staging offers a privacy solution for rental properties, for example if a tenant prefers not to have their personal belongings visible in public listing photos. (Talia Ricci/CBC)
Beyond furniture, differences between original and virtually staged images can change fundamental room characteristics, Singh said, as AI tools can alter wall moldings, room proportions and lighting.
Singh says those kinds of discrepancies can create unmet expectations during viewings and wasted time for both home seekers and agents.
Regulatory rules and transparency requirements

The Real Estate Council of Ontario (RECO) said in a statement that while AI is increasingly used in property marketing, its use must not alter a registrant’s obligations under the Trust in Real Estate Services Act. The act says "advertising must never be false, misleading, or deceptive."
RECO said consumers must be able to clearly identify when images have been virtually altered or AI-generated.

"That typically involves including a clear disclosure on the image itself or within the property listing," said a statement from Tess Lin, director of communications and stakeholder relations at RECO.
Fact check: Canadian real estate listings use AI-generated images
John DiMichele, CEO of the Toronto Regional Real Estate Board (TRREB), also stressed that virtual staging must maintain factual integrity.
“For instance, don't put lamps in a room that doesn't have outlets, unless you clearly say there are no outlets there,” DiMichele said.
CBC Toronto was able to find a number of active property listings in recent weeks that weren't clearly labelled on Realtor.ca. Such listings are then picked up on other real estate sites.
But DiMichele said that the majority of agents are following the guidelines.
Where AI staging is headed
The Ontario Real Estate Association said in a statement that as AI tools continue to develop, real estate organizations across Canada are actively establishing updated standards for usage.
Singh suggested those standards may need to expand beyond simple image labels.
“I do think that disclosure is a starting point. I think the next step might be even mentioning what tools were being used,” he said.

items: How artificial intelligence is changing the real estate game
More P.E.I. home listings are being advertised with virtual staging

blocks.text: For prospective buyers navigating current listings, he recommends being proactive.
"Buyers need to pay attention to the details, read the dimensions and the client remarks in the listings," he said.

Singh adds that if you're unsure whether a listing features virtual staging or how accurately it reflects the space, ask your real estate agent for clarification before booking an in-person viewing appointment.

Talia Ricci is a TV, radio and web reporter at CBC Toronto. She enjoys covering offbeat human interest stories and exposing social justice issues. Talia has also reported in London, Ont. and Winnipeg, Man. You can email story ideas to talia.ricci@cbc.ca.

articles.title: Burnham pledges ‘big changes’ to the way the welfare system works to tackle Neets crisis – UK politics live
articles.summary:
Prime minister’s comments come as children’s commissioner Dame Rachel de Souza highlights ‘staggering’ inequalities in young people’s treatment across UK

Good morning. Children and young…

blocks.text: Good morning. Children and young people are at the top of the agenda today, with the publication of a hard-hitting report from Dame Rachel de Souza, the children’s commissioner for England, and a Times article by Andy Burnham. They are focusing on slightly different cohorts – Burnham is writing about young people who leave school and enter the benefits system, while the de Souza reports covers the experiences of young children in multiple aspects of their lives – but their overall message is the same: the younger generation is being let down.

De Souza has studied more than 160 datasets to examine how what happens to children as they grow up varies across England and she says the variation is “staggering”. In her report, The Childhood Lottery, she explains:

double quotation markIn four local authorities, the total amount spent on youth services per teenager is the princely sum of £0, £421 less than in the highest spending local authority. Some areas of the country are sending nearly 90% of their looked after children to out-of-area placements, compared to the almost 20% in the areas making least use of these – although given this means being away from family ties, and friends, that is still worryingly high. But what stands out is not merely these differences, but how much work there is to do to deliver a happy, healthy childhood in every postcode. I have made the difficult decision to highlight the 20 places where it is hardest to grow up. I want to be clear that this is not a review of the local authority, this is an assessment based on a wide range of measures looking at the challenges faced, the full range of services available and the outcomes we see. We cannot shy away, though, from the fact that poor education outcomes, long health waiting lists or simply feeling unsafe converge in particular places.
The report identifies Middlesbrough as the most challenging place to be a child, and Cheshire East as the least challenging place. I will publish fuller tables shortly.
The overall picture is grim too. Here is an extract from the report’s summary.

double quotation markThe data pulled together in the Childhood Lottery highlights the scale of challenges faced by children across all areas of the country and all areas of their lives. For example that: -Over 1 million children (1,048,965) had active referrals to children and young people’s mental health services in 2024-25.1 -Most pupils (55%) do not achieve a good standard in their English and Maths GCSEs (grade 5 or better in both) at the end of key stage 4. -There are around 1 million young people in the UK aged 16 to 24 not in employment, education or training (NEET) -Approaching half (44%) of looked after children are placed outside their local authority area. Far too many care leavers (40%, plus 6% with unknown activity) are Neets [not in education, employment or training]. -12% of children said they did not feel safe in their local area.

The Burnham article is specifically about Neets. The government was expected to publish Alan Milburn’s final report with recommendations on Neets before the budget. Now it is coming next month, which means the pitch-rolling process ahead of publication is unusually protracted. Milburn has given an interview to the Guardian and, as Anna Bawden and Kiran Stacey report, he is explicit about wanting some benefit payments to be cut to fund more employment support.
In his article, Burnham accepts that many people people today feel “shut out”.

double quotation markThere is no shortage of people lining up to take a swing at the next generation but, if we are honest, the blame for this failure lies with politicians. At the very moment growing up became harder, the support young people relied on was stripped away. Youth services were practically abolished. Children’s mental health services were cut. Families were left to fight for support for children with special educational needs and disabilities. The pandemic stole two years, and social media is too often taking something much deeper: their confidence and sense of belonging. Add an education system focused on the university route and a job market offering too few opportunities, and we should not be surprised that so many are shut out.
And he signals that he is going to follow Milburn’s recommendations on benefits.

double quotation markToday, the welfare system provides an assessment, a payment and, after that, a goodbye. Too often there is no support, no offer of skills and no opportunity to get a job … This will be our offer: a clear guarantee of support. But it will also be matched by an expectation that young people will take up the opportunities made available to them. This will mean big changes to the way our welfare system operates. Benefits will become the backstop, not the starting point. The system will no longer begin by establishing which benefits a young person is entitled to. It will begin with their ambitions and the help they need to achieve them.
Here is the agenda for the day.
10am: Daisy Cooper, the Lib Dem deputy leader and Treasury spokesperson, holds a press conference on Lib Dem budget proposals.
Morning: Andy Burnham is on a visit in South Wales linked to the 60th anniversary of the Aberfan disaster (which is on Wednesday).
11.30am: Downing Street holds a lobby briefing.
2.30pm: Wes Streeting, the defence secretary, takes questions in the Commons.
3pm: Dame Rachel de Souza, the children’s commissioner for England, gives a speech at at the launch of her Childhood Lottery report.
After 3.30pm: MPs debate amendments to the Northern Ireland Troubles bill.
5.30pm: Rhun ap Iorwerth, the Welsh first minister, gives a speech on devolution.

I’m afraid we are no longer able to have comments open below the line every day on this blog. If you want to contact me, please email politics.live@theguardian.com. You can use this email to flag up corrections, comments for publication, questions or complaints.

articles.title: West Bank: Israel arrests 10 suspects over settler attacks on US journalist, European diplomats
articles.summary: Israeli police made the arrests following attacks on a US journalist and European diplomats in the occupied West Bank. Israeli human rights group Yesh Din has reported at least 170 settler attacks…

image.caption: The attack on veteran photojournalist Heidi Levine comes after global outrage over mounting settler violence in the West BankImage: Debbie Hill/UPI Photo/Newscom/picture alliance

blocks.text: Israeli police said Monday they had arrested 10 suspects over settler violence in the occupied West Bank, including attacks on a US photojournalist and European diplomats.
Masked settlers were filmed assaulting The Washington Post photographer Heidi Levine on Friday while she was covering a Palestinian olive harvest, leaving her with broken vertebrae.
The following day, settlers attacked a convoy of European diplomats and French mayor Bernard Baudoux, who was visiting the West Bank to help with the harvest.
The incidents drew condemnation from the United States, France, Belgium and Poland.
Israeli police said the investigation was ongoing, while Israeli media reported that the Shin Bet domestic security service was involved.
European diplomats attacked by Israeli settlers
What did the authorities say?

Major General Moshe Finchi, the Israeli police's West Bank commander, said "an arrest operation was conducted before dawn" following "the severe incidents of violence over the past weekend, including the assault of a media worker and the suspected attacks on foreign civilians."
Foreign Minister ⁠Gideon Saar and the Israeli military have blamed "Israeli rioters" for the attacks on the diplomats.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, however, said the diplomats entered a "sensitive area with a history of confrontations without prior coordination" ⁠with the Israeli military. He added that the facts of the attack on ⁠Levine were "unclear."
The attacks came ahead of the crucial October 27 elections for Netanyahu.
West Bank olive harvest under attack
Will the Israeli settlers face prosecution?
Settler violence against Palestinians has surged, with at least 170 attacks reported since September 27, according to Israeli human rights group Yesh Din.

DW's correspondent in Jerusalem, Tania Kraemer, said Palestinians, journalists and international observers have little confidence that the arrests will lead to charges against the alleged perpetrators.

Citing a study of Israeli police investigations into violence against Palestinians in the West Bank by Yesh Din, Kraemer said only about 3% of investigations between 2005 and 2023 ended in a full or partial conviction.
More than 80% were closed because police failed to identify suspects or gather sufficient evidence, the Yesh Din report said.
Israeli settler attacks on West Bank Palestinians increase

articles.title: Deepfakes, bots and distrust: How AI is shaping Israel's election
articles.summary: For the first time, AI is playing a major role in Israel's elections. Observers warn that deepfakes, bots and influence campaigns could sway voters.

image.caption: Netanyahu's Likud has used AI in its campaign more than any other major partyImage: Ohad Zwigenberg/UPI Photo/Newscom/picture alliance

blocks.text: In a 19-second clipposted to X, Gadi Eisenkot, a candidate for prime minister, stands with his arms outstretched and a huge smile on his face. In slow motion, he runs through a meadow toward a person who resembles his son, wearing a shirt with the words "Israeli Unity." But Eisenkot sails past him and instead embraces Mansour Abbas, a prominent Arab politician who leads the Ra'am party, running in the elections.

The video was posted on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's account. Opinion pollsshow Netanyahu and Eisenkot, who also happens to be a former chief of staff of the Israel Defense Forces, in a tight race. The AI-generated video appears to be designed to play on anti-Arab sentiment — a big part of Netanyahu's campaign.
The clip was viewed more than 1 million times and stirred outrage. Eisenkot's son was killed in 2023 during the Israel-Hamas war.

According to Ze Be AI, a research project of the Open University of Israel, monitoring AI content in the 2026 legislative election campaign, this clip is just one of more than 1,800 posts with AI-generated content that Netanyahu's Likud party had released throughout the election campaign by mid-October. That represents about a quarter of the Likud party social media materials analyzed by Ze Be AI.

blocks.caption: Netanyahu posted this AI-generated clip of rival Gadi Eisenkot on X in July. It was viewed more than 1 million timesImage: x.com/netanyahu

blocks.text: On October 27, Israelis will vote in an election that could oust Netanyahu from power or cement his grip on the country for the coming years. Political scientists are already calling it Israel's first AI election. Parties have been deploying AI across every aspect of campaigning — from creating outrageous videos aimed at stirring controversy to robocalling voters and unleashing bots online.

"There is a scenario where, in a strategic point shortly before the election, AI could or would be used in ways that would steer controversy that could tilt the election results," said Anat Ben-David, a media researcher leading the Ze Be AI project at the Open University of Israel.
AI videos go mainstream

Ben-David and her research team have been tracking all of the content posted on social media by politicians since the end of July. By mid-October, they had collected more than 44,000 posts across Facebook, Instagram, X and TikTok and found that over 14% of the material used AI in some way.
A hybrid approach was most common, with AI being deployed for a part or segments of an ad: in images, music, subtitles, logos or full-fledged deepfakes.

Some fringe parties use the greatest ratio of AI in their content. But Likud is the winner by far when it comes to sheer numbers of AI use in content analyzed by the team. Netanyahu's party is followed his left-wing rivals, the Democrats, and then Eisenkot's party, Yashar — though at far lower numbers.
Israel's Central Elections Committee issued a new rule in July mandating that all AI-generated or -manipulated content in election campaigning be labeled. Beyond that, there are few limits.
"There's no AI Act, no Digital Services Act, and the privacy law is very outdated," Ben-David said. "Then you see new [AI] uses that would be impossible to see in Europe."
Some of those uses have come from Israel's most prominent politicians.

Yair Golan, head of the Democrats, has been trying to capitalize on popular internet trends. One videolabeled as AI content features him sitting under a ceiling fan — with each rotation of the blade, his outfit changes: from an army uniform to a T-shirt with the popular slogan "bring them home now" (referring to Israeli hostages in Gaza) to a suit and tie.

In one photorealistic AI video, posted by Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich in September, Israel's attorney general and Supreme Court justices are apprehended at an anti-government protest. Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara has frequently clashed with the ruling coalition.

blocks.caption: An AI-generated video posted by Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich shows Israel’s attorney general and Supreme Court justices being detained at an anti-government protestImage: x.com/bezalelsm

blocks.text: And National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir shared an AI-generated video of Palestinians being wheeled on a conveyor belt into what looks like a concentration camp. That post drew widespread condemnation, with Germany's Foreign Ministry calling it"completely unacceptable" and "abhorrent."
The election authority has shown some willingness to intervene. In July, its chairman ordered Smotrich to take down an unlabeled AI video it called misleading.
A new generation of robocall
It's not just deepfakes and ads: AI is also being used to reach voters directly.

Some voters are getting a new kind of AI-powered robocall — far more conversational than the robotic automated calls of the past. Nitsan Yasur, a disinformation researcher at the Israel InternetAssociation, shared a recording with DW of a four-minute phone call.
Netanyahu's final campaign? — Israel heads to the polls

In it, a voice introduces itself as a pollster named Danielle with an Israeli polling institute and asks for his voting preferences. When Yasur asks if the voice is human, it admits, "there is no human agent on the line," before continuing to ask, "would you like to continue with the short survey?"

The bot fields several of Yasur's questions, while always steering back to who he would vote for. But when Yasur asks five times who commissioned the survey, it doesn't reveal the information. So it remains unclear whether this was part of an election campaign or a poll. What is clear is how advanced robocalling has become.
"You don't need real people making real phone calls, which are obviously limited in time and capacity," Tehilla Shwartz Altshuler, a senior fellow at the Israel Democracy Institute, told DW.
Efforts to shape what chatbots tell voters
Some Israelis are also turning to AI for advice on how to vote.
About a quarter of Israelis said they would consider using AI tools or other online services to inform their voting decisions, the Israel Internet Association found in a survey.

That raises concerns about generative engine optimization (GEO): creating online content designed to be picked up by AI chatbots and shape their answers. The Israeli government has already tapped this industry. According to filings under the Foreign Agents Registration Act, it paid a US firm to build websites meant to feed LLM systems with content supportive of the government in order to make AI chatbots more pro-Israel.
"The same industries are going to be used now inwards in order to affect the elections," she said.
Bot accounts promote Netanyahu online

There's fake content, and then there are fake audiences. Scooper, an Israeli company specializing in media monitoring, told DW that it discovered a network of inauthentic accounts boosting Netanyahu on social media. On X, more than 1,000 new accounts have been appearing daily and immediately following the Israeli prime minister. His Instagram following has also surged in recent weeks.

About 70% of the accounts that share Netanyahu's posts on X are based outside of Israel and resemble bots, Scooper research manager Gil Feldman told DW. Feldman said the company flagged them by looking for suspicious behavior such as round-the-clock posting, recent creation dates and missing profile pictures.
Israelis demand accountability for October 7

And it's not just Netanyahu: The Israeli watchdog FakeReporter found a bot campaign linked to Ben-Gvir's campaign, which his office denied. FakeReporter discovered a network of more than 100 accounts, some using AI-generated images and identities, targeting Smotrich and others.

Though bot networks are nothing new, AI can make them cheaper and easier to run. And, because Israelis are early and eager adopters of new technology, Shwartz Altshuler sees the country as a test case for how AI is reshaping elections around the world.
"The whole machinery of political propaganda is becoming totally different," Shwartz Altshuler said.

articles.title: Helen Haines updates: PM says person in custody after alleged attack on Helen Haines; police say she is in critical condition
articles.summary:
Independent MP injured in an incident involving a vehicle outside her electorate office in Wangaratta, in regional Victoria. Follow updates

‘No ongoing threat to community’: Victoria…

blocks.text: Victorian police release statement
Victorian police have released a statement, and said they have arrested a man who allegedly struck a women with a vehicle in Wangaratta.
Police say the woman – known to be Haines – is in hospital with “critical injuries”.
Police allege it was a white Toyota Landcruiser that struck Haines on Murphy Street at about 3.35pm, and that there was a knife seized from inside the vehicle.
The statement says:

double quotation markWhen he exited the Toyota, the driver, a 43-year-old Tarrawingee man, was arrested at the scene by a passerby. He will be interviewed in relation to the incident. The woman was taken to hospital with critical injuries. A knife was located by police and seized from inside the Toyota. At this stage, police are investigating as to whether this was an intentional act. It is not known yet if the parties are known to each other. Major Collision Investigation Unit detectives are en route. The investigation remains ongoing.
Key events

items: 10m agoVictorian police release statement
21m agoPM says suspect in custody after alleged attack on Haines
34m agoHelen Haines' family release statement

blocks.text: Acting Superintendent, Ashley Mason, says he was “not aware” of any prior concerns or incidents related to Helen Haines before today’s incident.
Asked how long the area will remain a crime scene, he says:

double quotation markWe’ve got our investigators from the Major Collision Investigation Unit who are currently en route to Wangaratta from Melbourne. So they’ve got significant travel time as well as the time it will take for them to thoroughly process the crime scene once they arrive. I think. There’s some talk that there might be specialist terrorist related police involved in the investigation. We’ve notified our crime and counter–terrorism command and they’re currently liaison and assisting our investigators.
‘No ongoing threat to community’: Victoria police
Mason tells journalists there is “nothing to indicate at this stage” that the two parties are known to each other, but police are still investigating.
He says there is no ongoing or further threat to the community or any other individual at this stage.

double quotation markI can provide some assurance to the community that we certainly do not have any intelligence that there is any further or ongoing threat to any other person or the broader community. We are treating this as an isolated incident at this point in time.
Acting Supt Ashley Mason is addressing the media in Wangaratta.
He says police are still investigating whether the incident was targeted.

double quotation markWe’ve still got a lot to work through here. As you can imagine, it’s been quite dynamic this afternoon. We’ve got quite an extensive crime scene. We have investigators present and they’ll continue to work through and try and collect all available evidence to ascertain exactly what has occurred and how it has occurred. We’ve got the Major Collision Investigation Unit who are currently en route from Melbourne.
Mason also will not confirm whether the incident was politically motivated.
Albanese is asked whether the government knew about any threats made towards Helen Haines.
Albanese says broadly, that he has called for the “temperature to be turned down” in political discourse.

double quotation markIt is too early, though, to speculate on motivation, and we won’t be doing so. We’ll allow the authorities to do their work. Obviously, Helen Haines has suffered … this is a serious incident, and so our thoughts are with Helen and her recovery at this time.
He’s also asked about what security measures were in place for Haines ahead of the incidence.
Albanese says security arrangements are made “based upon the threat levels which are there”.

double quotation markAnyone who looks at comments made and directed towards members of parliament and high office holders – there is increased heightened risk has occurred. Our thoughts are just very much with Helen, her family, her community at this time.
He ends the press conference there.
Albanese says his thoughts and his prayers are with Haines, her family and her community.

double quotation markHelen Haines is incredibly hard-working. She is fiercely intelligent, but most importantly, she’s just a thoroughly decent human being, full of integrity and respected right across the parliament, and from everyone who comes into contact with her, she is a well-loved member of her community, and this will come as an incredible shock to that community. Our thoughts remain with Helen Haines at this very difficult time.
The home affairs minister, Tony Burke, says there has been an increase in reports of harassing and threatening behaviour against MPs and their offices in recent years.
double quotation markThe year before last, we had 951 reports of harassing and threatening behaviour against various high office holders. The more recent financial year, that 951 has gone to 1,067.
PM says suspect in custody after alleged attack on Haines
Anthony Albanese is holding a press conference in Sydney, and says there is a major police investigation underway, and that a suspect is in custody.
He says the motive for the alleged attack is not known.

double quotation markThere is a major police investigation underway, and I can confirm that a suspect is in custody. The Australian Federal Police, Victorian Police, and Asio are working together on this. The joint counter-terrorism team has been activated, but the motive is not known.
Nationals frontbencher Michael McCormack, whose electorate shares a border with Haines’ has written on social media:
double quotation markSending my love and best wishes to Helen Haines for a full and speedy recovery. Such awful news.
Here’s what we know so far about the incident:
We’re expecting the prime minister and home affairs minister to speak shortly from Sydney.
Helen Haines' family release statement
Helen Haines’ family have released a statement to the media.
They have thanked bystanders, health workers and the police.

double quotation markThis afternoon, our beloved Helen was involved in an incident outside her Wangaratta Electorate Office, and is receiving medical care. We thank the swift assistance of bystanders and the dedicated health workers who assisted her, and police for their response. Our family, and Helen’s staff, will be making no further comment at this time, and ask that their privacy be respected by the public and media. Please keep Helen in your thoughts.

blocks.caption: Krishani Dhanji

blocks.text: Krishani Dhanji
Good evening, Krishani Dhanji with you here. We will be bringing you live coverage of the prime minister’s press conference, after an incident that has left independent MP Helen Haines injured.
The incident took place near her office in Wangaratta in regional Victoria.
Anthony Albanese and the home affairs minister, Tony Burke, will be speaking from Sydney shortly.

articles.title: Independent MP Helen Haines fighting for life after incident outside Wangaratta office in regional Victoria
articles.summary:
PM confirms a man is in custody after the Indi MP was left in a critical condition after being struck by a car on Monday afternoon

The independent MP Helen Haines has been critically injured…

blocks.text: The independent MP Helen Haines has been critically injured in an alleged attack involving a vehicle outside her electorate office in Wangaratta, in regional Victoria.

The prime minister, Anthony Albanese, confirmed on Monday night that a suspect was in custody and that the alleged attack on Haines was being investigated by the Australian federal police (AFP), Asio and the joint counter-terror taskforce.
He said the motive for the alleged attack was not known, and would not comment on whether the suspect was known to police.
In a statement, Haines’ family confirmed that she had been injured and thanked bystanders for their assistance.
“This afternoon, our beloved Helen was involved in an incident outside her Wangaratta Electorate Office, and is receiving medical care,” they said in the statement.
“We thank the swift assistance of bystanders and the dedicated health workers who assisted her, and police for their response.
“Our family, and Helen’s staff, will be making no further comment at this time, and ask that their privacy be respected by the public and media.
“Please keep Helen in your thoughts.”

In a statement, Victoria police said a 43-year-old man from Tarrawingee, about 10km from Wangaratta, was in custody and that a knife had allegedly been found in his car. They alleged he had been detained by a passerby when he exited the car.
The statement said the woman that was struck was in a critical condition.
“Police have arrested a man after a woman was struck by a vehicle in Wangaratta this afternoon.
“It is understood a white Toyota LandCruiser struck the 65-year-old woman outside an office on Murphy Street about 3.35pm.
Police said that they were investigating as to whether it was an intentional act, and it was not known if “the parties are known to each other”.
Emergency services had been called to the scene of the incident at Murphy Street on Monday afternoon.
According to the Victorian Emergency Services website, two vehicles responded and the road was closed after the incident.
In a social media post, the Nationals MP, Michael McCormack, said it was “such awful news”.
“Sending my love and best wishes to Helen Haines for a full and speedy recovery,” McCormack said.
Police were expected to release a statement regarding the incident on Monday night.
Haines has represented the electorate of Indi since 2019.
– More to come

articles.title: No Pinoys arrested or hurt in France unrest — embassy
articles.summary: The Philippine Embassy in France said that no Filipinos had been arrested and no casualties involving Filipino nationals had been reported amid the unrest in the country.

blocks.text: October 19, 2026 | 4:18pm

Police officers stand behind a fire near Place de la Republique following an unauthorised demonstration, central Paris, on October 18, 2026 a day after nationwide protests against the "high cost of living."
AFP / Matthieu Rondel
MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine Embassy in France said that no Filipinos had been arrested and no casualties involving Filipino nationals had been reported amid the unrest in the country.

In a statement on Sunday, October 18, the Philippine Embassy in France said that while it noted several violent incidents and cases of property damage in parts of France, including Paris, no casualties or legal detentions involving Filipino nationals had been recorded.

“Pinapayuhan ang mga Pilipino sa France na manatiling kalmado, iwasan ang mga lugar ng protesta at malalaking pagtitipon, at sundin ang mga tagubilin ng mga lokal na awtoridad,” the embassy’s statement read.
(Filipinos in France are advised to remain calm, avoid protest sites and large gatherings, and follow the instructions of local authorities.)
The embassy also reminded the Filipino community to maintain strict political neutrality, refrain from participating in local political disputes, and exercise restraint.

Filipinos residing in or visiting France were advised to follow all directives from local police, monitor official announcements regarding road closures and public transport disruptions, and ensure that family members were kept informed of their whereabouts.

The embassy also reminded the public to exercise caution on social media, verify information before sharing, and refrain from spreading unverified reports or inflammatory comments that could cause unnecessary panic.
Filipino nationals requiring urgent consular assistance may contact the Philippine Embassy in Paris through its dedicated hotlines and official channels:

items: Assistance-to-Nationals (ATN) Hotline: +33 6 80 11 52 71
Consular hotline: +33 6 20 59 25 15
Email: [email protected]

blocks.text: France has been experiencing civil unrest since September, with protests over the cost of living, fuel prices, and deteriorating public services.

The movement began as a month-long student protest over teacher shortages and poor school conditions, then broadened into anger over inflation, fuel prices, inequality, public spending cuts, and declining public services.
Trade unions, students, and groups linked to the “yellow vest” movement joined the mobilization.
On October 17, about 550,000 people marched nationwide, including 110,000 in Paris, according to the Interior Ministry, while organizers put the turnout at more than 800,000.

articles.title: Bangladesh says it was not informed of its citizens' execution by Saudi Arabia
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia said it executed two Bangladeshis last week for committing an "indecent act" in a mosque.

blocks.text: Bangladeshi authorities say they were not informed of the recent execution of two Bangladeshi nationals in the holy city of Mecca until after it had taken place, local media reports.

A Bangladeshi man and woman were executed last Wednesday after being convicted of committing an "indecent act" inside a mosque, according to the Saudi interior ministry. The ministry did not specify the nature of the offending act.
Bangladesh says it has reached out to the Saudi Arabian government to ask for more details about the case.
The two Muslim countries share a close relationship due to their religious affinity and strong economic ties.
More than three million Bangladeshis work and live in Saudi Arabia, mostly in low-paying jobs, and news of the double execution has raised public concern in Bangladesh.

According to the Saudi interior ministry, the two Bangladeshi nationals were convicted and sentenced to death under "tazir", which in Islamic law refers to punishments left to the discretion of the judge.
The ministry statement said they were handed the sentences because of the severity of the offence, and the fact that they violated the "sanctity" of the mosque.
Bangladesh has reached out to the Saudi government about the offences involved and legal proceedings in the case, said state minister for foreign affairs Shama Obaed Islam.
The government would consider next steps, such as the repatriation of the bodies, after getting information from Saudi authorities, Islam said.
She added that the government was committed to safeguarding the welfare and interests of Bangladeshis abroad.

The two executed Bangladeshis were included in a list of prisoners that Saudi Arabia had shared with Bangladesh, upon a request from the Bangladesh Consulate General in Jeddah - but that list did not indicate that the pair had been sentenced to death, the Daily Star reported.
This is not the first time that foreign nationals have been executed by Saudi authorities.
According to Amnesty International, the country has executed around 100 people this year, many of whom are foreigners convicted of drug offences.
In 2011, eight Bangladeshi men were publicly executed in the Saudi Arabian capital of Riyadh after they were found guilty of killing an Egyptian.

Earlier this month, Saudi Arabia overturned a death sentence handed to a Sri Lankan man over a comment he had made on Facebook, which had led to him being convicted of blasphemy. That decision came after the case sparked public outcry in Sri Lanka and spurred diplomatic efforts to seek clemency for the man.

articles.title: Marcos does not want Chinese ambassador expelled, says Palace
articles.summary: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has not signaled any intent to declare China’s ambassador persona non grata, the Palace said on Monday, October 19, though the Chinese diplomat today has been…

blocks.text: October 19, 2026 | 4:10pm

Secretary of Foreign Affairs Ma. Theresa Lazaro on Oct. 19, 2026 summons Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan to convey the Philippines’ serious concern and strong objection to his public statement of October 15, which conveyed a threat of the use of force.
Department of Foreign Affairs via Facebook

MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has not signaled any intent to declare China’s ambassador persona non grata, the Palace said on Monday, October 19, though the Chinese diplomat today has been officially summoned by the Department of Foreign Affairs.

“We know the president’s view. He would not want this kind of declaration, against any representative of another country here in our country,” Palace Press Officer Claire Castro told reporters in Filipino at a briefing. She was asked about calls from senators and congressmen to expel Ambassador Jing Quan.

On the same day, Foreign Affairs Secretary Theresa Lazaro formally summoned Jing and told him his October 15 remarks, said at a chance interview, were “provocative and unacceptable,” the DFA said in a statement.

The department also rebuked the Chinese embassy for its public attacks on lawmakers. It was “not the place of a foreign mission to publicly criticize or taunt Philippine officials and legislators who are acting within their mandates,” the DFA said. It reserved the right to take further diplomatic action, but did not say what that could involve or how Jing responded.
Castro said the Palace respected the views of lawmakers seeking Jing’s expulsion, but that Marcos would not go down this road as of yet.
“Everything he says can affect our country and our people,” she said.
The DFA has previously described declaring a diplomat persona non grata as an “option of last resort” that carries heavy diplomatic consequences.

JUST IN: Foreign Affairs Secretary Theresa Lazaro summons Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan to formally object to remarks he made last week, which the DFA says conveyed a threat of the use of force against the Philippines. @philstarnews https://t.co/QXpMwqYpwM — Cristina Chi (@chicristina_) October 19, 2026
‘We may easily win’

Jing made the remarks in question to reporters on the sidelines of a forum in Quezon City last week. Denying that China was a troublemaker, he said the Philippines should feel fortunate to have China as a neighbor. “If we want to use force, we may easily win,” he said, adding that China would not do so because it loves peace.
That evening, the DFA said the diplomat's words would seem to convey a “thinly veiled threat of the use of force."
Marcos reacted on October 16 and said the remark “sounds very much to me like a threat” and that he wanted to understand what the ambassador meant.

The embassy accused the DFA of selectively quoting and overinterpreting the ambassador. As senators called for Jing’s expulsion, the embassy dared them on Facebook: “Is this threat or coercion? But anyway, just do it. Otherwise, STOP BLUFFING.”
Sen. Erwin Tulfo earlier said the Senate majority plans to file a resolution seeking to have Jing declared persona non grata.
